questions.question: Which functional group is found in alcohols?
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl group (-OH) attached to a carbon atom. Examples include ethanol (CH3CH2OH) and methanol (CH3OH).

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name for CH3CH(OH)CH3?
questions.explanation: The -OH group is on the middle carbon (carbon 2) of the three-carbon propane chain. In the new IUPAC style, this would be propan-2-ol.

questions.question: What type of alcohol cannot be oxidized?
questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols lack a C-H bond on the carbon bearing the -OH, so they cannot be oxidized.

questions.question: What is the functional group of an ether?
questions.explanation: Ethers have two carbon groups bonded to an oxygen atom (R-O-R').

questions.question: Which of the following is a polyhydric alcohol?
questions.explanation: Ethylene glycol (HOCH2CH2OH) has two -OH groups, making it a polyhydric alcohol. It is used as antifreeze.

questions.question: What is the common name for diethyl ether?
questions.explanation: Diethyl ether is commonly called ethyl ether. It was historically used as an anesthetic.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct structure for glycerine?
questions.explanation: Glycerine (1,2,3-propanetriol) has three -OH groups attached to a three-carbon chain: HOCH2CHOHCH2OH.

questions.question: What type of bond links monosaccharides in disaccharides?
questions.explanation: Disaccharides like lactose and sucrose are linked by glycosidic (ether) bonds between monosaccharide units.
